body.p: Claims 1-22 are pending in the present patent application of which claims 1 and 12 are
independent claims. Claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 7-13, 15, 16 and 18-22 are amended in this paper. Claims
3 and 14 are canceled in this paper. No claims are added in this paper. By way of the current amendments, claims 1, 2, 4-13 and 15-22 would stand pending in the present application.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not

necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue any of the prior versions of the claims, any canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications and/or at a later date.
Applicant acknowledges with thanks the Examiner's indication of allowability of claims
3 and 14 upon overcoming the asserted indefiniteness rejections. (Office Action, p. 6).

Claims 1-22 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly "being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor ... regards as the invention." (Office Action, p. 2).
Without conceding the propriety of these asserted rejections, Applicant has amended the claims, as shown above, to address and overcome these asserted rejections. No new matter has been introduced.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of all 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) rejections of the claims.

Claims 1, 2, 5-7, 9-13, 16-18, and 20-22 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 2019/0021677 Al to Grbic et al. (hereinafter "Grbic"). (Office Action, p. 3). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

In this case, in the interest of advancing prosecution and to further distinguish over the cited art, Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 12, as shown above, to incorporate language from dependent claims 3 and 14, respectively, which the Examiner has indicated as being allowable. In view of these amendments, claims 3 and 14 have been canceled, as shown above. No new matter has been introduced.
As such, Applicant submits that Grbic fails to disclose, teach, or even suggest, each and every element of amended claims 1 and 12 and that claims 1 and 12 are thus allowable.

Claims 2, 5-7, 9-11 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1 and claims 13, 16-18, and 20-22 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 12. As discussed above, claims 1 and 12 are patentably distinguishable over Grbic for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 2, 5-7, 9-11, 13, 16-18, and 20-22 are patentably distinguishable over Grbic for at least the reasons discussed above, and because of the unique combination of limitations recited therein.
As such, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 102 rejections of claims 1, 2, 5-7, 9-13, 16-18, and 20-22.
Claims 4, 8, 15 and 19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being
unpatentable over Grbic. (Office Action, p. 5). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

Claims 4 and 8 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1 and claims 15 and 19 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 12. As discussed above, claims 1 and 12 are patentably distinguishable over Grbic for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 4, 8, 15 and 19 are patentably distinguishable over Grbic for at least the reasons discussed above, and because of the unique combination of limitations recited therein.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections of claims 4, 8, 15 and 19.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a

condition for allowance and respectfully solicits the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. The foregoing comments made with respect to the positions taken by the Examiner are not to be construed as acquiescence with other positions of the Examiner that may not have been explicitly contested. In addition, arguments presented herein for the patentability of a claim should not be understood as implying that no other reason for the patentability of the claim exists. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted,
